name: Exclamation Inflation (Punctuation Archaeology)
claim: Official congressional press releases carry about 50% more exclamation points per statement than they did in 2013 (0.032 rising to 0.048 across 2021-2026), and the earliest emoji found anywhere in the analyzable window landed on 2013-10-16 -- a description of the record, not a claim about what drove it.

numbers.metric: exclamation points per statement, per year (unicode scan of text_features.jsonl)
numbers.coverage_caveat: pre-2013 corpus coverage is too thin to claim the true first emoji/exclamation; all firsts are 'earliest in the 2013-2026 analyzable window', stated on the card's face

confounds_tested: true-first ambiguity -> NOT claimed: pre-2013 coverage too sparse, so the 2013-10-16 emoji is labeled 'earliest in-window', never 'first ever' (§consequence-1: pre-2013 retained only for descriptive artifacts, always with the coverage caveat)
symmetric trend claim -> NOT made: the +50% rate is a single-window aggregate description, not a two-party symmetric trend crossing 2013 backward
split_result: n/a -- descriptive single-window artifact, not a symmetric trend (per S2.4 protocol: 'No floor -- the receipt is the finding'). The exclamation curve and the earliest-emoji receipt are both measured strictly inside the 2013-2026 analyzable window; no claim crosses 2013 backward.
chart_spec: exclamation points per statement by year, 2013-2026 (single line), with the 0.032->0.048 endpoints annotated; inset/callout marking the 2013-10-16 earliest-in-window emoji as a dated receipt
receipts_note: receipts = the actual press releases behind the artifact: the 2013-10-16 emoji-bearing statement (member + date + url) and a sample of high-exclamation statements from the 2021-2026 tail, pulled from the phrase/statement index at publish time
republication_note: DESCRIPTIVE/reversal-candidate -- must be re-pre-registered in the found direction (rate rose ~50%; earliest-in-window emoji 2013-10-16) before publishing, per the parallel-session protocol.
